questions.q: What is the first move in setting a healthy boundary?
a: Say clearly and directly what your limit is
Wait quietly for the other person to notice
Drop hints and hope they catch on
Ask a third person to speak for you
questions.why: Lesson 1 says boundaries must be stated out loud, not assumed.

questions.q: What should you do when someone keeps ignoring a limit you set?
a: Apply a consequence and hold to it
Repeat the request more softly each time
Lower the limit to keep the peace
End every relationship in your life
questions.why: Lesson 2 says firm consequences protect limits that are repeatedly crossed.

questions.q: How does the summary say to decide between forgiving and walking away?
a: By weighing the person's intentions and the relationship's value
By counting how many years you have known them
By whether they apologize before you do
By what your family expects you to do
questions.why: Lesson 1 draws the line between forgiveness and foolishness.

questions.q: What does the summary warn about rigid boundaries?
a: They can make you seem cold and leave you lonely
They invite more people to test your limits
They are always healthier than flexible ones
They only work in workplace settings
questions.why: Lesson 3 says rigid limits isolate you, just as weak ones overwhelm you.

questions.q: Which questions does the summary recommend for self-reflection?
a: What am I comfortable with, and how do I want to be treated?
What would most people tolerate from a friend?
Which rules did my family follow growing up?
How can I avoid difficult conversations?
questions.why: Lesson 3 lists introspection questions about comfort and how you want to be treated.
